oidc_jwt.description: Successful JWT auth uses the configured user_claim string value as the identity entity alias name.
oidc_jwt.source: auth/jwt role docs: user_claim is used as the name for the Identity entity alias created due to a successful login
oidc_jwt.note: Display-name or alias differences from JWT sub are by design when user_claim is not sub.

oidc_jwt.description: Vault token lookup-self display_name may include an auth-mount-derived prefix before the upstream username/alias.
oidc_jwt.source: auth/token lookup-self sample response shows display_name like ldap2-tesla
oidc_jwt.note: Treat mount prefixes as platform metadata, not identity confusion.

oidc_jwt.description: Vault's OIDC provider does not support request or request_uri parameters.
oidc_jwt.note: Do not flag lack of request-object handling as a vulnerability on this provider.

oidc_jwt.description: JWT auth documentation does not describe jti tracking or one-time JWT consumption; replay of the same stateless JWT may be accepted if otherwise valid.
oidc_jwt.source: JWT auth API docs describe signature/claim validation but no jti replay cache
oidc_jwt.note: Per RFC 7519 this is generally hardening, not a vulnerability, for stateless JWT bearer auth.

oidc_jwt.description: Reusing the same upstream JWT for multiple login attempts is not documented as one-time or jti-tracked behavior for the JWT auth method.
oidc_jwt.source: Vault JWT auth method API docs describe signature/claim verification and token issuance, but no jti replay tracking.
oidc_jwt.note: Do not flag replay_same_token as a vulnerability for plain JWT bearer login unless another configured limit is violated.

oidc_jwt.description: An OIDC provider with empty allowed_client_ids allows no clients, while '*' allows all clients.
oidc_jwt.note: Authorization failures from empty allowed_client_ids are expected setup behavior, not audience-binding bugs.

oidc_jwt.description: An OIDC client with no assignments allows no Vault entities to authenticate through the client; allow_all must be assigned to permit all entities.
oidc_jwt.note: Authorization failures caused by missing assignments are by design.

oidc_jwt.description: Vault's built-in OIDC provider does not support request or request_uri parameters.
oidc_jwt.note: OIDC request-object alg=none tests are not applicable to this provider.

oidc_jwt.description: Vault's built-in OIDC provider supports only authorization_code flow with response_type=code.
oidc_jwt.note: Implicit/hybrid flow failures are by design, not security bugs.

oidc_jwt.constraint: configure_jwt_validation requires exactly one trust source: oidc_discovery_url, jwks_url, or jwt_validation_pubkeys. The fuzzer MUST set one and only one of these; setting none or multiple invalidates setup and breaks I1 trust-anchor tests.
configure_jwt_validation: bound_issuer cannot be configured when jwks_pairs is set. For I1 issuer-validation tests, do NOT use jwks_pairs if the test needs bound_issuer enforcement.
create_auth_role requires at least one bound value to be set. The fuzzer MUST include at least one of bound_audiences, bound_subject, or bound_claims; otherwise role creation/setup is invalid.

For jwt roles, bound_audiences is required when the JWT contains an aud claim and must match at least one associated aud value. For I5 audience tests, include bound_audiences on baseline roles; omitting it can make empty_audience or audience_mismatch tests uninterpretable.

bound_subject supports EXACT string match only; no wildcard companion parameter exists. A value like '*' is treated literally. For I4 multi-identity tests that need multiple sub values to authenticate to the same role, OMIT bound_subject entirely rather than trying to wildcard it.

bound_claims matching mode is controlled by bound_claims_type. Default bound_claims_type='string' means literal exact matching; glob wildcards only work when bound_claims_type='glob'. For I4/I5 multi-identity or wildcard tests, the fuzzer MUST set bound_claims_type='glob' before using '*' patterns; otherwise '*' matches only the literal asterisk string.

bound_claims accepts expected values as string, integer, boolean, or list of strings. Because the default bound_claims_type='string' treats values as literals and must match exactly, for I5 numeric coercion tests the fuzzer SHOULD set bound_claims_type='glob' so numeric claim values are coerced to strings rather than rejected outright.

user_claim must resolve to a STRING claim value. The alias name and resulting identity binding are derived from this claim. For I4 tests, do not use non-string claims for user_claim or login will fail for setup reasons rather than identity-binding reasons.

groups_claim must resolve to a LIST OF STRINGS. For I4 type-confusion group tests, Vault documents only list-of-strings as valid input; a scalar string groups claim may be rejected outright and should not be interpreted as a collision bug.

user_claim_json_pointer only changes how the claim path is interpreted; it does not change matching semantics. If using JSON pointer syntax in user_claim, the fuzzer MUST explicitly set user_claim_json_pointer=true or the claim lookup will fail for setup reasons.

Numeric sentinel semantics on JWT leeway fields: clock_skew_leeway value 0 means use default 60s, not strict zero; value -1 disables extra leeway. expiration_leeway value 0 means use default 150s, not strict zero; value -1 disables extra leeway. not_before_leeway value 0 means use default 150s, not strict zero; value -1 disables extra leeway. Never assume 0 means strict validation.

For I2 expired_token and future_token tests on jwt roles, account for default leeway sentinels. If the fuzzer leaves expiration_leeway or not_before_leeway at 0, Vault applies ~150s grace. To test strict expiry/nbf enforcement, set the relevant leeway to -1, not 0.

For I2 token-freshness tests against JWT login, the sequence MUST include a CONTROL login using a valid token alongside the ATTACK login. Otherwise LOGIN_FAILED on an expired/future token cannot be distinguished from broken trust-source, role, or claim setup.

For I1 issuer-validation tests, configure_jwt_validation MUST include bound_issuer. Without bound_issuer, Vault documents issuer comparison as optional and the test may pass trivially because issuer validation was never configured.

For I1 alg_none and resign_attacker_key tests, the fuzzer MUST configure an explicit trust source (jwks_url, oidc_discovery_url, or jwt_validation_pubkeys) and SHOULD constrain jwt_supported_algs. Otherwise failures or successes may reflect permissive algorithm defaults rather than the intended proof-integrity check.

jwt_supported_algs defaults differ by role type: OIDC roles default to [RS256], while JWT roles default to all available algorithms. For I1 algorithm-confusion tests on JWT roles, the fuzzer MUST set jwt_supported_algs explicitly to the intended allowlist; relying on defaults changes the attack surface.

For I3 config-change sequences, Vault role/config updates are BY DESIGN to affect NEW logins immediately. A valid coherence test must compare behavior of the same credential before and after the documented config change, not treat the admin change itself as a bug.

For I3 jwt_signing_key_rotation tests, rotate trust by updating configure_jwt_validation trust material (jwt_validation_pubkeys or jwks_url) and then retry login with the old key. Do not reuse stale baseline assumptions; the expected behavior is that new logins use the updated trust anchor immediately.

For I3 jwt_default_role_change tests, login_with_jwt may omit role and then uses default_role from mount config. The fuzzer MUST omit the role parameter on both baseline and post-change logins; supplying role explicitly bypasses the default-role behavior under test.
OIDC provider authorize endpoint requires scope to include openid and response_type=code. Tests that omit openid or use unsupported response types are invalid setup, not security findings.

Vault OIDC provider discovery advertises request_parameter_supported=false and request_uri_parameter_supported=false. Do NOT run oidc_request_object_alg_none against this provider endpoint; request JWT objects are not supported here, so rejection/absence is by design.

Vault OIDC provider discovery advertises grant_types_supported=['authorization_code'] only. Do NOT attempt RFC8693 token_exchange against /v1/identity/oidc/provider/{name}/token; token exchange is not documented/supported on this endpoint.

Vault OIDC provider discovery advertises token_endpoint_auth_methods_supported including none, client_secret_basic, and client_secret_post. Public clients use none and MUST use PKCE; confidential clients may use client_secret_basic or client_secret_post. The fuzzer must align client_type and token endpoint auth method or failures are setup errors.

Public OIDC clients MUST use PKCE for the authorization code flow. For public clients, start_oidc_auth must send code_challenge and exchange_code_for_token must send code_verifier. Missing PKCE on public clients is expected rejection, not an I3 bug.

Confidential OIDC clients MAY use PKCE but are not required to. For pkce_skip-style tests, distinguish public from confidential clients; rejection without code_verifier is mandatory only for public clients per the documented behavior.

OIDC token endpoint redirect_uri must exactly match the redirect_uri used when the authorization code was generated. For redirect_uri_mismatch tests, a non-200 rejection is expected and should be asserted via status code, not identity comparison.

OIDC client redirect_uris must exactly match the redirect_uri used in each authentication request. For I3/OIDC flow tests, ensure create_application includes the exact redirect URI used later; otherwise authorize/token failures are setup errors.

Vault OIDC provider docs say nonce is optional but strongly encouraged and is returned in the ID token nonce claim. For I2 replay-oriented OIDC tests, the fuzzer SHOULD always send a nonce and verify it in the returned id_token; omitting nonce weakens the test and may create false positives about replay handling.

OIDC provider allowed_client_ids semantics: empty means NO clients are allowed; '*' means all clients are allowed. Never treat empty as wildcard. For baseline OIDC provider setup, set allowed_client_ids explicitly or authorization will fail for setup reasons.

OIDC client assignments semantics: by default, no Vault entities are allowed to authenticate through the client. To allow all entities, supply the built-in allow_all assignment. The fuzzer MUST configure assignments appropriately or OIDC authorization may fail independently of the property under test.
OIDC scope name 'openid' is reserved in scope creation, and OIDC roles automatically include the standard openid scope. Do not try to create a custom scope named openid; use additional scopes only.

OIDC provider/client TTL fields are duration-or-int values, but no special 0 sentinel is documented for client access_token_ttl or id_token_ttl. Do not assume 0 disables expiry or means default unless explicitly documented elsewhere.

Identity alias cardinality warning: Vault documents that multiple authenticated entities can be bound to the same alias and thereby gain access to all of its privileges. For I4 collision tests, alias reuse is a real documented risk surface; the fuzzer should inspect alias names and mount accessors carefully rather than assuming uniqueness is enforced.

Entity merges fail when entities contain aliases sharing the same mount accessor unless conflicting_alias_ids_to_keep is provided, and such merges must be one-at-a-time. For I4 collision investigations, do not interpret merge failures as proof of safe identity separation; they are documented merge constraints.

Group alias creation requires the auth mount accessor, not the mount path. The fuzzer MUST obtain and use the correct accessor value for the JWT/OIDC auth mount when mapping external groups; using a path string will break setup.

External identity groups are populated via group aliases from auth methods. For JWT/OIDC group-policy tests, create an external group plus group alias rather than relying on manual member_entity_ids if the intent is to model upstream group claims.

Group policy application mode can be within_namespace_hierarchy or any. In Enterprise, if mode=any, group policies apply across namespace boundaries. For I5 group_policy_escalation tests, namespace effects must be accounted for or cross-namespace policy inheritance may look like escalation but be by design.

KV v2 config sentinel semantics: max_versions=0 means keep the default 10 versions, not zero versions. delete_version_after='0s' means no automatic timed deletion, not immediate deletion. Never assume these zero values are literal strict-zero behavior.
verify_read_secret on KV v2 MUST use the /data/ path segment. Using /v1/{engine}/{path} hits KV v1 shape and returns misleading 404s unrelated to authorization.

KV v2 list operations use /metadata/ paths, not /data/. If the fuzzer needs list capability during setup or verification, grant/list against /metadata/ explicitly; otherwise list failures are policy-shape issues, not auth bugs.

Token use-budget analysis: token num_uses=0 means unlimited uses, not zero uses. Any nonzero use budget is consumed by EVERY API call made with that token, including verify_granted_identity and verify_read_secret. Minimum safe value is 2 if the sequence performs one self-inspection call before one protected-resource read; use 3+ if additional verification calls are present.

For I5 identity_policy_override and group_policy_escalation tests, remember that Vault tokens can carry both token policies and identity/group-derived policies. The oracle must compare granted permissions against role intent plus documented identity/group policy mechanisms, not just auth role token policies.

configure_jwt_validation requires exactly one trust source: set ONE AND ONLY ONE of oidc_discovery_url, jwks_url, or jwt_validation_pubkeys. Do not send multiple trust anchors in the same config update or setup will be invalid.

For I1 issuer-validation tests, configure_jwt_validation MUST include bound_issuer. The docs mark bound_issuer optional; if omitted, Vault will not compare the JWT iss claim and issuer-substitution tests become meaningless.
bound_issuer cannot be configured when jwks_pairs is set. Do not use jwks_pairs for issuer-enforcement tests that need bound_issuer.

create_auth_role requires at least one bound value to be set. A role with no bound constraints is invalid setup. For jwt roles with an aud claim, bound_audiences is required and the JWT aud must match at least one configured audience.

bound_subject supports EXACT string match only. There is no companion bound_subject_type parameter. Wildcards like '*' are treated literally, not as patterns. For I4 multi-identity tests that need multiple sub values to pass the same role, OMIT bound_subject entirely rather than setting it to '*'.

bound_audiences is exact list-membership matching against JWT aud claims; no wildcard or glob mode is documented. For cross-provider or multi-client tests, do not use '*' as a wildcard audience. Either configure the exact expected audience(s) or omit the constraint when the scenario requires multiple different audiences to pass.

user_claim is not a matcher; it selects which claim becomes the entity alias name, and the claim value must be a STRING. For I4 tests, choose a stable string claim such as sub. Non-string claim values will not work as alias names.

groups_claim is not a matcher; it selects which claim becomes group alias names, and the claim value must be a LIST OF STRINGS. For type-confusion tests, string vs list behavior is security-relevant because non-list values are not valid group claims.

bound_claims supports string, integer, boolean, or list-of-strings expected values. Matching mode is controlled by bound_claims_type. Default bound_claims_type='string' means literal exact matching; bound_claims_type='glob' enables '*' wildcard matching.

For I4 multi-identity scenarios using bound_claims, exact-match mode will only admit the literal configured values. If the test needs multiple different identities to pass the same role, either OMIT the relevant bound_claims entry or explicitly set bound_claims_type='glob' with a deliberate pattern. Do not assume '*' works unless bound_claims_type is set to 'glob'.

For I5 numeric coercion tests on bound_claims, set bound_claims_type='glob' rather than the default 'string' so non-string JWT claim values are coerced to strings for matching instead of being rejected outright by literal string handling.
clock_skew_leeway has sentinel semantics: value 0 means use the default 60 seconds, not literal zero; value -1 disables extra leeway. Never assume 0 is strict checking.
expiration_leeway has sentinel semantics: value 0 means use the default 150 seconds, not literal zero; value -1 disables extra leeway. Never assume 0 disables expiration or enforces strict expiry.
not_before_leeway has sentinel semantics: value 0 means use the default 150 seconds, not literal zero; value -1 disables extra leeway. Never assume 0 is strict nbf enforcement.

For I2 expired_token and future_token tests against jwt roles, include a CONTROL login using a valid token in the same setup. Because leeway defaults are nonzero (60s/150s/150s when set to 0), an attack token near the boundary may still be accepted by design unless leeway is explicitly set to -1 or the timestamps are moved well beyond the default buffers.

JWT replay with the same bearer token is stateless by design for Vault's jwt login unless constrained by token issuance settings; do not treat reuse of the same upstream JWT as an I2 vulnerability by itself. Focus freshness tests on exp/nbf/iat enforcement and issued Vault token limits instead.

For I3 config-change tests, new logins after modify_role_config or configure_jwt_validation are expected to use the NEW configuration. A valid coherence test must show that the same stale credential is rejected or re-bound under the updated config, not that an admin change legitimately altered future behavior.

default_role on /auth/{mount}/config controls login_with_jwt behavior when role is omitted. For jwt_default_role_change tests, omit the role parameter on login_with_jwt; if you send an explicit role, the default_role change is bypassed and the test is invalid.

OIDC auth_url and callback are stateful. exchange_code_for_token must use the exact state, nonce, and optional client_nonce from the preceding start_oidc_auth flow. Mixing values across sessions will test state binding, not normal login.

Vault's OIDC callback requires nonce as a request parameter in addition to state and code. The fuzzer must preserve and replay the nonce from the auth_url flow; omitting it causes setup failure unrelated to the target invariant.

For OIDC upstream tests, public clients MUST use PKCE: code_challenge is required at authorize time and code_verifier is required at token time. Confidential clients may omit PKCE. Do not interpret public-client rejection without code_verifier as a bug.

OIDC provider discovery for Vault's built-in provider advertises request_parameter_supported=false and request_uri_parameter_supported=false. Do NOT attempt request-object or request_uri based attacks against this provider; alg=none request-object tests are not applicable here.

Vault provider discovery advertises response_types_supported=['code'] and grant_types_supported=['authorization_code'] only. Do not test implicit or hybrid flow behaviors against the built-in provider.

allowed_client_ids on /identity/oidc/provider is exact client-id allowlisting except for the documented sentinel '*', which means all clients are allowed. Empty allowed_client_ids means NO clients are allowed. Never treat empty as wildcard.

OIDC client assignments default to denying all Vault entities. To allow authentication through a client, configure assignments explicitly; to allow all entities, use the built-in allow_all assignment. A missing assignment can cause false-negative login failures unrelated to JWT/OIDC validation.

redirect_uris on /identity/oidc/client must EXACTLY match the redirect_uri used in each authorization request. For redirect mismatch tests, ensure the baseline uses an exact configured URI first; otherwise failures are just bad setup.
UserInfo endpoint requires Authorization: Bearer <access_token>. When using OIDC token responses, session_token for downstream API calls must be access_token, not id_token.
KV v2 verify_read_secret must use the /data/ path segment. Using /v1/{mount}/{path} hits KV v1 semantics and returns misleading 404s.
KV v2 list capability is on /metadata/, not /data/. If a policy only grants read on /data/, list operations will fail by design. Do not misinterpret that as authorization inconsistency.

KV v2 engine config has sentinel semantics: max_versions=0 means keep the default 10 versions, not zero versions; delete_version_after='0s' means no automatic deletion. Never assume 0 means immediate deletion or no retention.

Any token-use budget parameter such as num_uses/token_num_uses counts EVERY API call made with that Vault session, including verify_granted_identity and verify_read_secret. Minimum safe value is 2 if the sequence performs both self-lookup and a protected-resource read; use 3+ if additional session-inspection calls are included.

Group aliases are the documented way to map external JWT/OIDC groups into Vault identity groups. For group-policy escalation tests, create an external identity group and bind it via create_group_alias using the auth mount accessor; direct group membership alone does not simulate external group claims.

Group policy application mode is globally configurable. Default mode within_namespace_hierarchy restricts when identity-group policies apply; mode any applies group policies regardless of namespace hierarchy. Cross-namespace group-policy tests must account for this global setting or they will produce false positives/negatives.

configure_jwt_validation: bound_issuer cannot be configured when jwks_pairs is set. For issuer-validation tests, do NOT use jwks_pairs; use oidc_discovery_url, jwks_url, or jwt_validation_pubkeys so bound_issuer can be enforced.
Numeric sentinel semantics: clock_skew_leeway uses special sentinels. value 0 = use default 60 seconds, NOT literal zero; value -1 = disable added leeway. Never assume 0 means strict checking.

Numeric sentinel semantics: expiration_leeway uses special sentinels. value 0 = use default 150 seconds, NOT literal zero; value -1 = disable added leeway. Never assume 0 means immediate expiry enforcement with no buffer.

Numeric sentinel semantics: not_before_leeway uses special sentinels. value 0 = use default 150 seconds, NOT literal zero; value -1 = disable added leeway. Never assume 0 means strict nbf enforcement.

Numeric sentinel semantics: KV v2 engine config max_versions uses special sentinel 0 = keep 10 versions (platform default), NOT zero versions. Do not use 0 expecting immediate deletion of all history.
Numeric sentinel semantics: KV v2 delete_version_after uses special sentinel "0s" = do not schedule automatic deletion. Do not interpret "0s" as immediate deletion.

Session-use budget: token_num_uses limits every API call made with the session token, including verify_granted_identity and verify_read_secret. If the sequence performs both self-lookup and secret-read, minimum safe token_num_uses is 2; use >=3 if any extra session-authenticated verification call is added.

bound_subject supports EXACT string match only; there is no companion bound_subject_type. Wildcards like '*' are treated literally. For I4 multi-identity tests, OMIT bound_subject entirely rather than setting it to a wildcard.

user_claim must resolve to a STRING claim value. If the selected claim is non-string, login will fail before identity-binding tests run. For I4 tests, choose a string-valued claim such as sub or another stable string claim.

groups_claim must resolve to a LIST OF STRINGS. A scalar string groups claim is not equivalent and will fail type validation. For I4/I5 group-mapping tests, test string-vs-list type confusion explicitly because Vault documents list-of-strings only.

bound_claims matching mode is controlled by bound_claims_type. Default bound_claims_type=string means literal exact matching; glob mode enables '*' wildcard matching. For multi-identity scenarios that need multiple different values to pass the same constraint, either set bound_claims_type=glob with an intentional pattern or OMIT the constraint entirely. Do not set bound_claims={'sub':'*'} under default string mode because only the literal '*' will match.

bound_claims accepts string, integer, boolean, or list-of-strings expected values. For I5 numeric coercion tests, set bound_claims_type=glob (not the default string) so that numeric claim values are coerced to strings rather than rejected outright.

For I2 expired_token and future_token tests on JWT roles, account for default leeway unless you explicitly set expiration_leeway and not_before_leeway to -1. Otherwise tokens slightly outside exp/nbf may still be accepted by design because Vault adds default 150s leeway when the fields are 0/unset.

For I2 token-freshness tests, include a CONTROL login using a valid JWT alongside the attack JWT. Without a control, LOGIN_FAILED on the attack token cannot be distinguished from broken trust-source or role configuration.

For I1 algorithm tests, jwt_supported_algs should be explicitly narrowed to the expected trusted algorithms. JWT roles otherwise default to all available algorithms, which can make algorithm-confusion tests ambiguous.

For I3 config-change tests, re-login after modifying /auth/{mount}/config or /auth/{mount}/role is the correct oracle. Vault documents that config and role updates take effect on subsequent logins; do not treat changed behavior after an admin update as a bug unless the SAME stale request is inconsistently evaluated.

OIDC auth flow: allowed_redirect_uris on the role must contain the exact redirect_uri used during the flow. Redirect URI matching is exact; mismatches cause flow failure and are not evidence of a security issue.

OIDC auth flow: public clients MUST use PKCE. The provider docs state code_challenge/code_verifier are required for public clients and only optional for confidential clients. Do not flag missing-PKCE rejection for public clients as a bug.

OIDC auth flow: nonce is documented as optional but strongly encouraged and is returned in the ID token nonce claim. For replay-oriented OIDC tests, always send a nonce and verify the callback flow uses the matching nonce; omitting nonce weakens the test oracle.

Vault OIDC provider discovery explicitly advertises request_parameter_supported=false and request_uri_parameter_supported=false. Do NOT run OIDC request-object tests (including alg=none request parameter attacks) against this provider endpoint; unsupported request objects would yield false positives.

Vault OIDC provider discovery advertises response_types_supported=[code] and grant_types_supported=[authorization_code]. Do not attempt implicit or hybrid flow tests against the provider endpoints in this documentation set.

Vault OIDC provider client assignments default to denying all Vault entities. To allow authentication through a client, configure assignments explicitly or use the built-in allow_all assignment. Otherwise authorization failures are expected setup failures, not security findings.

Vault OIDC provider allowed_client_ids on the provider defaults to allowing NO clients when empty; '*' allows all clients. For provider-side tests, an empty allowed_client_ids list is deny-all by design, not wildcard.

Vault OIDC provider token endpoint supports only authorization_code grant_type. Do not attempt RFC 8693 token_exchange against /v1/identity/oidc/provider/{name}/token; token exchange is not documented for this endpoint.
KV v2 access tests must use the /data/ path segment for reads and writes. Using /v1/{mount}/{path} hits KV v1 semantics and will produce incorrect 404/permission results on KV v2 mounts.
KV v2 list capability is on /metadata/ paths, not /data/ paths. If you grant list permissions for setup or verification, include the metadata path explicitly or list operations will fail by design.

Identity group alias creation requires the auth mount accessor, not the mount path. The provided docs for this protocol run do not document a mount-accessor lookup endpoint, so get_mount_accessor is absent-in-docs and must be sourced externally if group alias tests are executed.

External identity groups are intended to receive memberships via aliases from auth methods. For JWT/OIDC group-mapping tests, prefer type=external groups plus create_group_alias rather than manually populating member_entity_ids, or the test may not reflect real broker behavior.

Group policy application mode can change authorization semantics across namespaces. Default mode is within_namespace_hierarchy; mode any relaxes this and applies group policies regardless of namespace hierarchy. Cross-namespace group-policy escalation tests must record the current /sys/config/group-policy-application mode before asserting I5 outcomes.
